uk.title: Flag of the United Kingdom (Union Jack)

colors.note: The field; represents the sea and naval tradition. Also the blue of St Andrew's Saltire for Scotland.
The crosses of St George (England) and St Patrick (Ireland); represents military strength and valour.
Fimbriations and the Cross of St Andrew (Scotland); represents peace and honesty.

desc:
- The Union Jack combines the red cross of St. George (England), the white saltire of St. Andrew (Scotland),
- and the red saltire of St. Patrick (Ireland) on a blue field. The current design was adopted on 1 January 1801
- following the Acts of Union with Ireland. It is one of the world's most recognizable flags
- **Construction:** the Union Flag combines the crosses of St George (red on white, England), St Andrew (white saltire on blue, Scotland), and St Patrick (red saltire on white, Ireland)
- The red saltire is offset (counterchanged) so it does not overlap the white saltire, preserving symmetry
- The flag has no official standard; convention uses 1:2 or 3:5

countryData.name: United Kingdom
countryData.officialName: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

trivia:
- The Union Jack is asymmetric — the red diagonal stripes are offset (counterchanged) so as not to overlap the white Scottish saltire
- The flag combines the crosses of St. George (England), St. Andrew (Scotland), and St. Patrick (Ireland)
- The Union Jack dates to 1801 and represents the unity of the United Kingdom
